Button.defaults: Button defaults to the secondary variant and sm size. Set variant="primary" explicitly for the main action. Its default HTML type is button; use type="submit" to submit a form.
guidance: Choose a short label that names the result, such as Save booking or Add traveler. Use Button for an action and TextLink for navigation.
Use primary for the main action, brand for an outlined work action, and secondary for a supporting action. Use danger for destructive actions and ConfirmDialog when confirmation is needed.
Use the existing xs, sm and md sizes. The size sets label typography, spacing and control height together. fullWidth fills the available container; it does not change the label style.

typography.description: Button uses the Action label role. The font family and weight stay consistent; the selected size sets the text size. Keep these shared styles when building product screens.

icons: Use leadingIcon before the label to reinforce an action, such as plus with Add traveler. Use trailingIcon after the label to indicate a direction or next step.
Choose either icon slot, both, or neither in the controls. Icons inherit the button color and are decorative when the visible label already explains the action.
Use IconButton for an icon-only action and provide an aria-label that describes its purpose. Browse the Icons page for the complete icon set.
accessibility: Keep a visible, meaningful label. Save booking describes the action; Click here does not. The visible text supplies the button's accessible name.
Use Tab to focus an enabled button, then Enter or Space to activate it. Keep the visible focus indicator so keyboard users can find the current control.
For an icon-only action, use IconButton with aria-label, for example Close booking details. A decorative icon beside a visible label does not need a second accessible name.
Set loading while the application is processing an action. Button exposes aria-busy and prevents repeated activation; the application must manage the request and success or error feedback.
Disabled buttons cannot be activated and are skipped by normal Tab navigation. Explain an unavailable action beside the control instead of relying on a tooltip on the disabled button.
Button defaults to type="button". Set type="submit" explicitly for a form's submit action, and retain type="button" for actions such as Cancel.
